topics.title: Value Types, Reference Types, ref & Nullability
topics.summary: Reason precisely about copying, aliasing, nullable reference analysis, structs, readonly data, and by-reference APIs.

concepts.name: Value versus reference
concepts.explanation: Struct values are copied by value; class variables copy references to objects. This semantic distinction matters more than memorizing “stack versus heap” shortcuts.

concepts.name: ref family
concepts.explanation: ref, in, out, ref readonly, ref returns, and ref locals allow code to alias storage rather than copy values. These tools improve specific APIs but increase lifetime/aliasing complexity.

concepts.name: Nullable references
concepts.explanation: Nullable reference types add compile-time flow analysis. string and string? express different nullability intent, but the feature does not magically prevent every runtime null.

topics.challenge: Create a readonly struct and pass at least one struct argument with in/ref readonly semantics; also demonstrate one nullable reference.
topics.hint: Focus on semantics: readonly struct protects mutation, while in avoids copying/communicates readonly by-reference intent in suitable APIs.

references.title: Microsoft Learn — Reduce allocations and copies

topics.title: Advanced Interfaces, Abstractions & API Contracts
topics.summary: Design stable abstractions with interfaces, generic contracts, default/static interface members where appropriate, and explicit dependency direction.

concepts.name: Interface evolution
concepts.explanation: Default interface members can add implementation to interfaces, but they change design tradeoffs and should not become a substitute for coherent base abstractions.

concepts.name: Static abstract members
concepts.explanation: Modern C# interfaces can require static abstract members, enabling generic algorithms over operator-like capabilities and powering generic math patterns.

concepts.name: Dependency direction
concepts.explanation: High-level logic should depend on contracts that describe needed behavior. Keep interfaces focused enough that implementations can satisfy them honestly.

topics.challenge: Create an interface with a static abstract member and a generic method constrained to that interface.
topics.hint: Static abstract interface members are consumed through a constrained type parameter, not an interface instance.

references.title: Microsoft Learn — Generic types and methods

topics.title: Task Coordination, Cancellation & Concurrent Design
topics.summary: Compose asynchronous operations under cancellation and failure while distinguishing I/O concurrency from CPU parallelism.

concepts.name: Cancellation tokens
concepts.explanation: CancellationToken is cooperative: pass it through layers and check or forward it to APIs that support cancellation.

concepts.name: Task coordination
concepts.explanation: Task.WhenAll, WhenAny, SemaphoreSlim, and channels/queues solve different coordination problems. Avoid starting unbounded work just because async makes it easy.

concepts.name: CPU versus I/O
concepts.explanation: Async improves nonblocking waits; it does not automatically make CPU-heavy work parallel. Parallelism uses threads/cores and has separate synchronization costs.

topics.challenge: Write an async workflow that forwards CancellationToken and limits concurrency with SemaphoreSlim or a similar gate.
topics.hint: The concurrency limit should wrap each operation with WaitAsync in try/finally so the permit is always released.

topics.title: Reflection, Attributes & Runtime Metadata
topics.summary: Inspect type metadata, annotate code with attributes, and invoke discovery-based behavior without losing sight of compile-time alternatives.

concepts.name: Attributes
concepts.explanation: Attributes attach metadata to assemblies, types, members, parameters, and more. Attribute classes derive from System.Attribute.

concepts.name: Reflection
concepts.explanation: System.Reflection can inspect types, members, generic arguments, attributes, and sometimes invoke members dynamically.

concepts.name: Tradeoffs
concepts.explanation: Reflection is flexible but reduces compile-time visibility and may have trimming/AOT/performance implications. Source generation or explicit registration can be better for hot paths and deployment-sensitive code.

topics.challenge: Create a custom attribute, apply it to a type, and read that attribute through reflection.
topics.hint: Derive the attribute from Attribute and limit its valid targets with AttributeUsage.

topics.title: Testing, SOLID Tradeoffs & Maintainable C# Design
topics.summary: Design testable code by separating pure logic from effects and apply design principles as tradeoff tools rather than rigid slogans.

concepts.name: Test seams
concepts.explanation: Inject clocks, storage, HTTP clients, or repositories behind narrow abstractions when deterministic tests need control over those dependencies.

concepts.name: Single responsibility
concepts.explanation: A type should have a coherent reason to change. Splitting every three-line method into a new class is not automatically better design.

concepts.name: Dependency inversion
concepts.explanation: High-level policy should not be forced to construct low-level infrastructure. Constructor/function injection makes dependencies explicit and replaceable.

topics.challenge: Create a service that receives one dependency through its constructor and uses that abstraction instead of constructing the dependency internally.
topics.hint: The constructor should clearly show what the service needs in order to do its work.
